clue.text: See great difference in cheap travel

indicators.note: a difference in the letters means the words see and great are made different by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A remark that cheap travel shows a great difference from the luxury kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difference in' signals the anagram of SEE and GREAT together, eight letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage was the cheapest class of passenger accommodation on a ship, so it stands for budget travel.

clue.text: Panic about the cold when short

indicators.note: about means the fright word goes round the cold symbol

parts.note: a scare is a panic
C stands for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Fear sets in about the cold when supplies run low.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is in short supply.

clue.text: Send out without a drink

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone sent away without a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To export is to send goods out of a country for sale.

clue.text: Note a boy's sound thinking

parts.note: re is a note of the sol-fa scale
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Observe that a lad is thinking clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason is rational, logical judgement.

clue.text: West Indian islands producing grains need organisation

indicators.note: the letters of grains need are organised into a new order

explanation.surface: The Caribbean islands produce cereals that need organising.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grenadines are an island chain in the Caribbean, part of St Vincent and the Grenadines.

clue.text: Mother's got a little house in the country, lucky thing!

parts.note: mother is MA, so mother's is MA'S
a cot is an old poetic word for a small cottage in the countryside

explanation.surface: Mum owning a country cottage is seen as a stroke of good fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a charm or creature kept to bring good luck to a team or group.

clue.text: Cut short a game with small daughter

parts.note: bridge is a card game
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A game was shortened because of a little girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Abridged means condensed, shortened.

clue.text: Jam to use sparingly

explanation.definitionFit: A conserve is a fruit preserve, and to conserve is to economise.

clue.text: The bank concerned with backing up America in venture

indicators.note: in places the middle pieces inside the attempt word

parts.note: a try is an attempt, a venture
re means about, concerning

indicators.note: backing up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: USA is America

explanation.surface: A bank that supports American enterprise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Treasury is a government department holding public funds, the nation's bank in effect.

clue.text: Characters all requiring really good punt

parts.note: alpha is the top grade in marking, so it means first-rate
a punt is a gamble, a bet

explanation.surface: Everyone involved needs a sure-fire wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' is not the boat here but the informal British word for a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: An alphabet is the complete set of letters used in writing a language.

clue.text: Appear submissive or have a ding-dong in church?

indicators.note: in places the bell-ringing inside the abbreviation for the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
ding-dong is the sound of bells, so to ring

explanation.surface: Asks whether one should cower or start a row while in church.
explanation.walkthrough: A ding-dong is also British slang for a noisy quarrel, the surface sense; here it is the sound of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: To cringe is to shrink back or cower in a fearful, servile way.

clue.text: Bodily stripes this guy has!

definitions.meaning: an army non-commissioned officer wearing two chevrons on the sleeve

explanation.definitionFit: Corporal means physical as an adjective, and a corporal is a junior army rank marked by two stripes.

clue.text: Publicity about the German calculators

indicators.note: about means the publicity word goes round the German article

parts.note: ads, advertisements, are publicity
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Advertising surrounding German-made calculating machines.
explanation.definitionFit: An adder is a machine or circuit that adds numbers, so a calculating device.

clue.text: Cleaners will be put off vulgar men

parts.note: to deter is to put off
gents is a colloquial, common form of gentlemen

explanation.surface: Coarse men will be discouraged by cleaning staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Detergents are cleansing agents.

clue.text: He's always prepared to compromise a jailbird

definitions.meaning: an opportunist who adapts views to suit the times

explanation.definitionFit: A timeserver bends to prevailing opinion for advantage, and read literally names a convict serving a sentence.

clue.text: Give voice about prison getting the news first

indicators.note: about means the singing word goes round the prison word

parts.note: to sing is to give voice
coop is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Singing about jail to break a story ahead of rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop is an exclusive story, so scooping is reporting it before competitors.

clue.text: Great-grandfather, for instance, eats corn only if well cooked

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of eats corn are prepared in a new order

explanation.surface: Grandpa eats sweetcorn only when it is thoroughly cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-grandfather is one example of a forebear.

clue.text: A measure taken in fiction to ensure natural growth

indicators.note: taken in means the measure is put inside the fiction word

parts.note: a lie is a fiction
a metre is a measure of length

explanation.surface: A step taken in a story to promote organic growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A lime tree is a linden, something that grows naturally.

clue.text: Thought to bamboozle subordinate, plainly inflamed

parts.note: to con is to trick or bamboozle
side as an adjective, as in a side issue, means secondary
red is the visible colour of inflamed skin

explanation.surface: An idea to trick an underling who is visibly angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Considered as a past participle means pondered, reflected upon.

clue.text: One's immersed in water — there's no trick in it

indicators.note: immersed in puts the one's piece inside the water word

parts.note: a mere is a lake
one is I, so one's is I'S, read as IS

explanation.surface: Someone is plunged into water, and there is no trick to it.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games such as solo whist, misère is a bid to win no tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A misère bid is a declaration to take not a single trick.

clue.text: A six-footer's fantastic throne

indicators.note: fantastic means the letters of throne are rearranged fancifully

explanation.surface: Someone's extraordinary royal seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six-footer' suggests a tall person, but an insect has six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornet is an insect, and insects have six legs.

clue.text: This will provide cover for the viewer

definitions.text: This will provide cover for the viewer

parts.words: This will provide cover for the viewer
parts.note: viewer is the eye, and the cover is the fold of skin that closes over it

explanation.definitionFit: The skin fold that shuts over the eye, protecting the organ of sight.

clue.text: Light food offered in the home — lettuce maybe

indicators.note: offered in says the dish is sitting within the words home and lettuce

explanation.surface: A light meal served at home, perhaps with a side of lettuce.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette, here in the American spelling, is a light egg dish.

clue.text: Plant border in a bad way

indicators.note: in places the edge inside the suffering word

parts.note: to be in agony is to be in a bad way
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A garden border looking in poor condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant border' reads as a flowerbed, but 'Plant' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrimony is a yellow-flowered herb of the rose family.

clue.text: Having a half of bitter in a hostelry, shut up!

indicators.note: in places the beer fragment inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry

indicators.note: a half of the word bitter, its closing three letters, as a half pint of bitter

explanation.surface: Ordering a half of bitter in the pub, and being told to be quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut up!' is not an order for silence but means 'imprison!', as to intern is to confine.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern someone is to confine or detain them, especially in wartime.

clue.text: Conclude article backing the left will be seen as vile

parts.note: to infer is to conclude

indicators.note: backing means the article is written in reverse

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Concluding that a newspaper piece supporting the political left is disgraceful.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal literally means hellish, hence detestable or wicked.

clue.text: Information given about a road in a pleasant area

indicators.note: about means the information word goes round the road pieces

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Details are provided about a road that runs through a nice district.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden is a cultivated, agreeable plot, the very type of a pleasant spot.

clue.text: Insisted upon a dessert being properly served

indicators.note: the words a dessert are laid out again in a new order, as dishes are arranged for serving

explanation.surface: A diner demanded that a pudding be served correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: To have asserted something is to have stated it forcefully, maintaining it.
